articles.title: Ferrocene heteroconjugation enables charge transport in DNA monolayers
Near-infrared plasmonic response in hyperdoped silicon nanoantennas for all-silicon photodetection
articles.abstract: Abstract Plasmonic materials enable subwavelength confinement of light through the collective response of free carriers, but their operational spectral range is typically constrained by intrinsic carrier densities. Hyperdoped semiconductors offer a route to engineer plasmonic properties within a CMOS-compatible platform, yet their plasmonic response in silicon remains largely limited to the mid-infrared. Here we show that nanoantenna engineering extends the plasmonic response of phosphorus-hyperdoped silicon toward the near-infrared. The nanoantenna arrays exhibit tunable, polarization-dependent resonances in the 1–2 μm range, arising from geometry-driven localized modes on a Drude-like electronic background. Leveraging these effects, we realize all-silicon photoconductive detectors operating at 1.55 μm and room temperature, with a maximum bias-assisted responsivity of 0.58 A/W at 0.5 V. This response arises from plasmon-enhanced sub-bandgap absorption combined with trap-assisted photoconductive gain and therefore does not represent the intrinsic quantum efficiency. These results extend the spectral functionality of silicon photonics beyond its intrinsic absorption limits for integrated sensing, imaging, and optical communication.

articles.title: UMIche: a UMI-centric analysis platform for enhancing molecular quantification accuracy in bulk and single-cell sequencing
articles.abstract: Abstract Unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) are widely utilised in RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) technologies to eliminate polymerase chain reaction (PCR) duplicates, thereby improving the accuracy of molecular quantification. However, synthesis errors in UMIs during sequencing often compromise the reliability of UMI counting. While various computational methods have been developed for error correction, the lack of a unified benchmarking and validation framework impedes systematic evaluation and optimisation. Here, we present UMIche, an open-source, UMI-centric computational platform designed to enhance UMI-assisted molecular quantification. Its application to collapsing monomer and homotrimer UMIs across multiple bulk and single-cell sequencing protocols demonstrates effective PCR-duplicate removal. Across a broad spectrum of simulated and experimental datasets with ground truth, most UMI collapsing methods integrated into UMIche perform similarly under low-error conditions, whereas set-cover optimisation and majority voting show greater robustness as the UMI error profile becomes more pronounced. Together, these capabilities enable scalable UMI collapsing, systematic benchmarking, and method development to improve molecular quantification.

articles.title: Topographical mismatch sustains open microchannels in living soft tissue for non-destructive protein biopsy
Low-thermal-budget solution-processed montmorillonite dielectric for low-voltage 2D electronics
articles.abstract: Abstract Low-voltage and high-performance electronic devices based on two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors demand high-quality dielectrics with efficient capacitive gating. However, it currently relies on specially engineered atomic layer deposition (ALD) of ultrathin high- k HfO 2 and ZrO 2 , or high-temperature vapor-phase growth of 2D dielectrics with post-growth transfer process. Here, we report a facile solution-processed 2D dielectric with an ultra-low thermal budget (i.e., at room temperature), while delivering competitive device metrics (e.g., low operating voltage and small hysteresis). This is enabled by an organic-free colloidal ink of montmorillonite (MTM) in environmentally friendly water solvent, eliminating the need for organic ligands or surfactants and thus the post-deposition high-temperature thermal annealing. Specifically, all-solution-processed MoS 2 field-effect transistors with MTM dielectric exhibit a low operating voltage of 1 V and small hysteresis (down to 1 mV). The solution process is generally compatible with diverse n-type and p-type 2D semiconductors such as MoS 2 , MoSe 2 and WSe 2 . Moreover, the robust and reproducible MTM dielectric enables scalable device integration into logic circuits, including inverters, AND, NOR, and NAND gates, as well as static random-access memory (SRAM). The scalable room-temperature solution-processed 2D dielectric offers a route to all-solution-processed and low-voltage 2D electronics.

articles.title: High-pressure synthesis of a polymeric N3H2 solid stabilized by hydrogen bonds
articles.abstract: Abstract Polymeric nitrogen represents a long-sought class of high energy density materials, in which single-bonded nitrogen networks release large amounts of energy upon decomposition to molecular N 2 . However, polymeric nitrogen allotropes require extreme pressures to synthesize and cannot be recovered at ambient conditions due to surface instabilities. Hydrogen has been proposed as a key element to stabilize such frameworks, yet polymeric nitrogen–hydrogen solids have until now remained the realm of theoretical calculations. Here, we report the high-pressure synthesis of polymeric N 3 H 2 at 134(3)–139(1) GPa from N 2 –H 2 mixtures. Synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy and first-principles calculations reveal a fully single-bonded framework of 1-dimensional chains of N 6 rings, each decorated by four H atoms. The chains of N 6 H 4 units are cross-linked through hydrogen bonds. Employing modern synchrotron sources, hydrogen positions are directly resolved from diffraction data at 139(1) GPa. At ambient conditions, N 3 H 2 exhibits an estimated energy of decomposition of 7.98 kJ/g, highlighting hydrogen-stabilized polymeric nitrogen as a promising class of energetic materials.

articles.title: Experience modifies the synaptome architecture in the developing and adult mouse brain
articles.abstract: Abstract Synaptome architecture describes the spatiotemporal distribution of highly diverse excitatory synapses throughout the brain. Whether and how this architecture is impacted by experience and sensory input is unknown. We found that environmental enrichment and monocular visual deprivation drive large-scale reconfiguration of excitatory synapse populations in more than one hundred regions of the mouse brain. Different experiences modify distinct subsets of synapse types and subtypes, with patterns aligned with protein turnover rates and connectome architecture. Similarity in experience-dependent reconfiguration during development and adulthood indicates shared mechanisms of synaptome adaptation across the lifespan. Our findings support a population-selection model in which experiences drive adaptation by selectively modifying synapse types and subtypes distributed across the brain. Experience-driven reconfiguration of synaptome architecture shares features with the response to aging, sleep deprivation, brain injury and genetic mutations, supporting a unifying principle of brain adaptation.

articles.title: Functionally divergent RHOA mutations drive peripheral T cell lymphoma development by engaging a common neomorphic pathway
Frequency-tagged fMRI reveals dual mechanisms of attentional enhancement and suppression
Processing-induced self-organised triboelectric interfaces enable event-responsive cementitious composites
Toward triggered generation of indistinguishable single photons from MoTe2 quantum emitters
Pharmacological chaperone treatment with Cystadane in aspartylglucosaminuria: an open-label, phase Ib/II trial
articles.abstract: Abstract This phase Ib/II investigator-initiated, open label trial aims to show the safety and efficacy of Cystadane (betaine) in aspartylglucosaminuria, a lysosomal storage disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline, in Finnish patients homozygous for the Finnish major mutation, aged between 3 and 17 years at study begin (recruited: 25, analyzed: 21). Oral Cystadane efficacy and safety were studied over 48 months. The primary endpoint of the study, reduction of glycoasparagines in the urine, was quantitatively determined using liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry and normalized to urine creatinine. Urine glycoasparagines are significantly reduced upon Cystadane treatment (by 68.6% ±10.8%; p = 0.000), and the study thus meets its primary endpoint. Our data show that Cystadane/betaine efficiently improves the main disease biomarker, and it is safe to use in aspartylglucosaminuria. Further studies should be carried out in a larger patient population over a longer time to demonstrate the effects on disease progression. EudraCT registration number 2017-000645-48.

articles.title: OsCPK17- and OsMPK6-mediated dual phosphorylation of OsPUB12 maintains OsPUB2-regulated OsPUB12 homeostasis and balances rice immunity

Multitechnique Characterization
of Dissolved Organic
Matter from Naturally Acidic and Circumneutral Waters Reveals Molecular
Controls on Organic Nitrogen Speciation
articles.abstract: Abstract The molecular characteristics of dissolved organic matter (DOM) vary across seasons, catchments, and land uses, highlighting the need for generalized structure–function relationships that can predict intrinsic DOM bioavailability. This study characterized DOM from naturally acidic (pH 4.3–5.7) and circumneutral (pH 6.8–8.3) freshwaters over two seasons: winter-spring (WS) and summer-autumn (SA) using multiple characterization techniques (optical, fluorescence, targeted LC-MS/MS, 13C NMR, and FTIR). DOM from acidic environments was higher in aromaticity, more humic-like, with a higher C:N ratio but with a greater percentage of nitrogen in the form of amino acids (i.e., DCAA-N%). Seasonality was only observed for neutral samples, with differences between WS and SA dominated by a decrease in nominal molecular weight (MWn) in SA, likely driven by photochemical disaggregation. FTIR analysis indicates that neutral DOM has a higher amide group abundance than acidic DOM despite the lower DCAA-N%, suggesting the dominance of nonproteinaceous amide-N. Very strong dependencies were observed for dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) speciation against aromaticity (SUVA254) and an FTIR-derived ratio of deprotonated carboxylic:aromatic groups, describing the relative hydrophilicity–hydrophobicity of the DOM environment. These parameters largely explain the DCAA distribution and may provide a more generalized way of characterizing DOM that could be applied across different aquatic ecosystems.

articles.title:
Toward
Dynamic Biointerface Toxicology of Micro- and
Nanoplastics Using Organoids and Organ-on-a-Chip Models
articles.abstract: Abstract Micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) toxicity depends on the exposure conditions under which particles encounter biological tissues, yet nominal material descriptors alone do not resolve these conditions. Environmental transformation, biomolecular adsorption, aggregation, and chemical release can alter particle delivery and biological interactions. This Review evaluates these processes alongside evidence from organoids and organ-on-a-chip models, distinguishing direct MNP findings from analogue studies and demonstrations of platform capability. We propose exposure identity as an analytical framework connecting particle history and state with tissue encounter and subsequent processing over time. The synthesis examines what available studies establish about tissue access, barrier responses, distal relay, and susceptibility, and where interpretation remains constrained by exposure characterization or unresolved mechanisms. Human-derived models provide opportunities to investigate tissue-specific responses, but neither biological complexity nor perfusion establishes environmental representativeness or predictive validity. We identify measurement and control requirements for separating particle transfer from chemical release and tissue-derived signaling, interpreting absent effects, and evaluating heterogeneous exposures. Priorities include traceable delivered-dose measurements, synchronized exposure and response sampling, targeted mechanistic tests, and independent validation for a defined use. The proposed framework organizes evidence and testable relationships while retaining uncertainty about generalization to human exposure and health outcomes.

articles.title:
Missed
Opportunities Forgo One-Third of Mass Timber’s
Carbon Storage Potential
articles.abstract: Abstract Building materials are increasingly positioned as a scalable option for carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Carbon-storing engineered wood products, such as structural mass timber, will be instrumental for CDR. However, system-level perspectives can overlook operational choices that forfeit storage potential. Using stage-resolved life-cycle inventories, scenario-aware uncertainty analysis, and dynamic carbon accounting, we trace carbon flows across mass timber supply chains in the United States, from harvest slash and mill residue to wood products through end-of-life. Across modeled deployment scenarios, we show that management decisions, not technical limits, cut 1.4–2.6 gigatons (Gt) of CO2e storage by 2120, corresponding to roughly one-third of mass timber’s storage potential. Globally, storage losses from these choices could reach 3.8–12 Gt CO2e. We outline a storage-first pathway including slash pyrolysis, diversion of mill residue from bioenergy to wood panel markets, and reuse or pyrolysis at end-of-life. Together, these strategies redirect carbon into value-added, long-lived pools rather than short-lived fates, showing that release timing and supply chain routing choices can matter more than production decarbonization in shaping warming outcomes under mass timber deployment. If implemented, these choices recover forgone storage and aid in developing the built environment as a durable carbon reservoir.

articles.title:
Contrasting
Dynamics of Particle-Bound Organophosphate
Esters Reveal Distinct High-Altitude Contaminant Transport Processes
over the Tibetan Plateau
articles.abstract: Abstract Particle-bound semivolatile organic compounds (SVOCs) reaching high-mountain regions are commonly interpreted in terms of temperature-driven gas-particle partitioning and precipitation scavenging. To investigate these competing dynamics, we report year-round, synchronous measurements of particle-bound organophosphate esters (OPEs) in PM2.5 at two contrasting Tibetan Plateau sites: a southern Himalayan receptor (QOMS) and an inland background site (NAMORS). ΣOPEs averaged 111 ± 125 pg m–3 at QOMS and 20 ± 17 pg m–3 at NAMORS, exhibiting a counterintuitive warm-season maximum. This warm-season peak coincided with a 72–91% decline in hygroscopic secondary inorganic aerosols, indicating that trans-Himalayan transport sustains substantial particle-bound OPE inputs during the monsoon despite intense wet deposition. Furthermore, chlorinated congeners with stronger particle association (TCPP, TDCPP) dominated at both sites (TCEP/TCPP = 0.09–0.46). This contrasts with the highly volatile TCEP-dominated profiles reported for Arctic aerosols. Such a difference is consistent with an orographic modulation favoring particulate-phase retention during the shorter trans-Himalayan ascent. However, the lack of simultaneous gas-phase data and potential differences in regional emission histories must also be acknowledged. Back-trajectory clustering and principal component analysis both point to South Asian source regions as the principal control at QOMS. Consequently, correlations of OPEs with temperature and precipitation are better read as proxies for monsoon transport intensity than as evidence of local thermodynamic partitioning. Continued transboundary input suggests that particle-bound OPEs may contribute to deposition and subsequent accumulation in the alpine cryosphere, highlighting the urgent need to incorporate transboundary transport pathways into regional contaminant assessments.

articles.title:
Organophosphate
Flame Retardants Induce Neurodegenerative
Pathologies by Paralyzing HSP90AB1 Chaperone Function: A Multi-Scale
Computational and Biophysical Study
articles.abstract: Abstract This study integrated computational toxicology with biophysical and cellular validation to investigate the neurotoxic potential of 10 flame-retardant-related compounds. ADMETlab 3.0 predicted blood-brain barrier probabilities of 0.989 for bis(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate and 0.444 for diphenyl phosphate (DPHP), interpreted as screening predictions. Network topology analysis identified HSP90AB1 as a shared candidate hub target linking organophosphate flame retardants to Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated a stable HSP90AB1 backbone in the DPHP complex (root-mean-square deviation ∼0.18 nm). Surface plasmon resonance measured an equilibrium dissociation constant of 1.49 μM. DPHP induced dose-dependent cytotoxicity in neuronal cells; the half-maximal inhibitory concentration was not determined within the tested range. HSP90AB1 overexpression mitigated DPHP-induced reactive oxygen species production and transcriptional upregulation of pro-apoptotic and pro-inflammatory genes. Single-cell virtual knockout identified candidate regulatory processes; Parkinson’s disease-related enrichment remained exploratory after multiple-testing correction. Together, the computational, biophysical, and cellular findings support HSP90AB1 as a candidate target of environmental neurotoxicity and motivate further investigation of DPHP.

articles.title:
Tire-Derived
Organic Pollutants across Urban Land
Uses: Associations with Traffic Exposure
articles.abstract: Abstract Tire-derived organic pollutants (TDOPs), particularly N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) and its transformation product 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), are increasingly recognized as emerging urban contaminants. However, their distribution and potential drivers in urban soils beyond the immediate roadside environment remain poorly characterized. In this study, 19 TDOPs were quantified in 28 urban soil samples representing four land-use types in Metro Detroit, Michigan, United States. TDOPs were widely detected in all soil samples, and 16 compounds exhibited detection frequencies ≥75%. Very low 6PPD/6PPD-Q ratios and the relative enrichment of N,N′-diphenyl-p-phenylenediamine (DPPD) over 6PPD suggest substantial environmental transformation of 6PPD. No statistically significant differences in the concentrations of TDOPs among land-use types or associations with measured soil properties were detected. In contrast, 6PPD exhibited a strong positive association with traffic-derived exposure metrics. The maximum Spearman rank correlation coefficient was observed for the commercial traffic exposure metric at a distance-decay parameter of 800 m (ρ = 0.76), and the association remained significant after optimization-adjusted permutation testing (pperm = 0.00030) and false discovery rate correction (q = 0.0048). This study demonstrates the widespread occurrence of TDOPs in urban soils beyond the immediate roadside environment and identifies modeled traffic exposure as an important correlate of soil 6PPD concentrations.

articles.title:
Redox-Active
Electrodes Enable Selective Ammonium
Recovery and Reuse for Rare Earth Mining
articles.abstract: Abstract Rare earth element (REE) extraction from ion-adsorption deposits relies on ammonium (NH4+) assisted in situ leaching, yet the spent leachant is typically discarded as wastewater rather than recovered for reuse. Here, we report a redox-active electrosorption platform that selectively recovers NH4+ from REE tailings wastewater and enables its direct reuse in the leaching process, establishing a circular approach to nitrogen management. This platform employs nickel-substituted copper hexacyanoferrate as redox hosts for reversible ammonium storage. Nickel incorporation modifies the redox and ion-transport properties of CuHCF while improving framework stability. The resulting Cu0.8Ni0.2HCF redox-active electrode exhibits a high capacity of 82.6 mAh g–1, superior cycling durability (>90% retention after 30 h), and remarkable ammonium selectivity over Na+ (9.2), Ca2+ (19.3), Mg2+ (25.5), La3+ (38.5), and Y3+ (42.2). Multiscale characterizations and calculations support favorable NH4+ host–guest interactions and ion transport within the framework. The recovered ammonium is directly reused for ion-adsorption-type rare earth leaching with extraction performance comparable to fresh leachants. Life-cycle assessment and techno-economic analyses demonstrate reduced environmental footprint and favorable economic feasibility. This study established a redox-active electrosorption platform that shifts nitrogen management from a linear “treatment-discharge” model toward a circular “recovery-reuse” pathway.

articles.title:
Electron Transfer
Pathways Stretching from the Extracellular
to Intracellular Membrane in Biohybrids Enable Enhanced CO2 Upcycling to Malate
articles.abstract: Abstract Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) empowers one-step conversion of CO2 to long-chain chemicals under mild conditions, enabling sustainable biomanufacturing and achievement of a circular carbon economy. Although the construction of biohybrids has been explored to enhance the inherently low efficiency of MES, whether the binding modes between nanomaterials and microorganisms dictating CO2 conversion efficiency remain elusive. To address this query, we constructed biohybrids with three distinct integration modes (namely, internalization, outer membrane-contact, and transenvelope) between nanomaterials and Shewanella, enabling to proceed CO2-to-malate conversion. Upon MES-driven CO2-to-malate conversion, the transenvelope biohybrid constituted by polydopamine and Shewanella achieved a marked gram-scale malate titer of 19.14 mmol/L, as a result of the distinctive transenvelope capacity of polydopamine stretching from the extracellular to the intracellular membrane. This transenvelope capacity imparts extended electron transfer pathways spanning from the cytoplasmic membrane to the extracellular space, significantly reducing interfacial barriers at the electrode-microorganism interface and greatly promoting NADH and ATP synthesis for malate synthesis, which can enhance NADH synthesis. This work proposes the construction of a transenvelope biohybrid to optimize microbial metabolism, offering an alternative for the efficient valorization of CO2 to carbon-negative long-chain chemicals.

articles.title:
Non-Targeted
Characterization and Hazard-Based Prioritization
of Disinfection Byproducts and Co-Contaminants in U.S. Drinking Water
Distribution Systems
articles.abstract: Abstract Higher-carbon (>C2) disinfection byproducts (DBPs) remain poorly characterized in drinking water distribution systems (DWDSs) despite evidence that they may contribute substantially to drinking water toxicity. Here, we applied liquid chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry and non-targeted analysis to characterize >C2 DBPs and co-contaminants across 12 U.S. DWDSs spanning a range of pre-oxidation and disinfection strategies. For each DWDS, we analyzed finished drinking water and distribution system samples collected at locations representing short, medium, and long distances from the treatment plant. We identified multiple classes of >C2 DBPs, including non-halogenated and halogenated hydroxybenzoic acids, halohydroxybenzaldehydes, halonitrophenols, (halo)phenylacetamides, (halo)fumaric acids, and several emerging nitrogenous DBPs. In addition, we also detected various co-contaminants such as pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and industrial chemicals. DBPs and co-contaminants exhibited system-specific occurrence and spatial patterns, and non-halogenated hydroxybenzoic acids emerged as an overlooked and widespread class of DBPs. To support prioritization efforts, hazard data from EPA’s Hazard Comparison Module was used to develop and implement hazard-weighted prioritization metrics. This approach identified (halo)hydroxybenzoic acids, halonitrophenols, DEET, triazine herbicides, and 2-hydroxyquinoline as high-priority contaminants, indicating that both emerging DBPs and co-contaminants may contribute to mixture-level hazards in distributed drinking water. Overall, this work expands the known >C2 DBP landscape and provides a framework for prioritizing drinking water contaminants detected by non-targeted analysis.

articles.title:
Biomass
Hydrothermal Reduction Enables Direct Copper
Recovery from Wastewater
articles.abstract: Abstract Recovering copper (Cu) from strongly acidic copper wastewater (SACW) is essential for resource sustainability and environmental preservation, but conventional technologies bear high economic costs and generate secondary pollution. Here, we demonstrate a biomass waste-mediated hydrothermal reduction process that simultaneously removes and recovers Cu as metallic Cu from SACW. The process operates under mild conditions (180 °C, 7 h) and achieves over 99% removal of Cu(II) across a wide concentration range, directly reducing Cu(II) to metallic Cu(0) without incorporation into hydrochar. Notably, the liquid products from biomass hydrothermal treatment, particularly 2-furoic acid, served as electron donors for Cu(II) reduction, with its C2/C3 atoms potentially providing electron transfer channels that drive the stepwise reduction of Cu(II) to Cu(0). In a 5 L pilot test with two types of industrial wastewater, the technology achieved >99% Cu(II) removal (residual <0.5 mg/L) and recovered metallic Cu with a purity of 99.9% after simple calcination. Life-cycle assessment and technoeconomic analysis highlight superior economic and environmental benefits when treating high-concentration copper-containing wastewater, establishing a sustainable, generalized hydrothermal reduction platform for efficient Cu recovery from industrial wastewaters. This work establishes a chemistry-driven paradigm for sustainable wastewater treatment, enabling efficient circular recovery of high-value resources from acidic metal-containing wastewaters.

articles.title:
Emerging Hexafluoropropylene
Oxide Trimer Acid Potently
Targets Farnesoid X Receptor and Triggers Hepatic Cholestasis
articles.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) hepatotoxicity is a critical global health threat, and disrupted bile acid metabolism is considered a key driver of PFAS-triggered liver injury, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Herein, we explored the hepatotoxic mechanisms of emerging hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA) and dimer acid (HFPO–DA) via farnesoid X receptor (FXR), assessed their health risks, and further compared their effects against perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). In rat, HFPO-TA exerted more potent hepatotoxicity than PFOA and HFPO–DA, triggering typical cholestasis through impaired biliary excretion and altered bile acid pool. Mechanistically, all three PFASs promoted the intracellular bile acid accumulation by inhibiting FXR transcriptional activity, with potent HFPO-TA > PFOA > HFPO–DA. Accordingly, HFPO-TA, HFPO–DA, and PFOA can directly bind to FXR though entering the ligand-binding domain via hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions to stabilize an antagonizing conformation. Notably, HFPO-TA bound FXR with 3.25-fold higher affinity than endogenous chenodeoxycholic acid and 50-fold higher affinity than PFOA, accompanied by elevated receptor-bound concentrations (RBCs). RBC-based risk assessment revealed moderate risk in 28.3% of HFPO-TA-exposed residents. Overall, HFPO-TA directly binds to FXR to induce hepatic cholestasis; such FXR-mediated cholestasis poses notable health risks and warrants broad vigilance toward PFAS liver hazards.

articles.title: A national baseline for methane sink habitats and methanotroph diversity
A lactate-fatty acid loop drives prostate cancer bone colonization by mediating metabolic interplay between tumor cells and osteoblasts
articles.abstract: Abstract Bone metastasis is the major cause of morbidity and mortality in advanced prostate cancer, yet current therapies provide only limited clinical benefit. Here, we show that prostate cancer cells metabolically adapt to the bone microenvironment by utilizing bone-cell-derived lactate as an alternative nutrient source. Beyond fueling oxidative phosphorylation, lactate serves as carbon source for fatty acid synthesis. Among the resulting lipid products, oleic acid is secreted to reward osteoblast, establishing a reciprocal metabolic interplay that supports both tumor progression and pathological bone formation. Mechanistically, we identify MCT1 as the essential transporter mediating lactate uptake in bone-colonizing tumor cells. MCT1 expression is coordinately regulated by NFAT signaling and extracellular glucose availability at both transcriptional and post-translational levels. Genetic deletion and pharmacological inhibition of MCT1 markedly suppresses prostate tumor growth in bone. Together, these findings uncover a lactate-driven metabolic crosstalk, identifying MCT1 as a promising therapeutic target for prostate cancer bone metastasis.

articles.title: Conserved molecular properties of dissolved organic matter during Weddell Sea Deep Water formation
articles.abstract: Abstract Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) is decreasing in volume due to climate change with potential consequences for abyssal carbon storage, where carbon is locked away from the atmosphere for centuries. Understanding the formation and export of dissolved organic matter (DOM) on the Antarctic shelf is therefore essential to determine how organic carbon enters this deep-sea reservoir. Here, we investigate solid-phase extractable DOM (SPE-DOM) transformations in the Weddell Sea, where half of AABW forms. Molecular and structural properties of SPE-DOM remain unchanged during dense-water formation. Shelf processes minimally affect exported organics into the deep-sea, likely due to remineralization to inorganic carbon enhanced by long residence times on the shelf. Consequently, the dominant SPE-DOM signature in Weddell Sea Deep Water (WSDW) is established before dense shelf waters mix with warmer off-shelf waters. We estimate that 0.155 ± 0.03 PgC are transferred annually from the Weddell Sea to AABW, and that its molecular composition is expected to remain conserved despite ongoing climate-driven weakening of AABW.

articles.title: Electric vehicle battery materials supply disruptions can be mitigated  with chemistry changes and recycling
Global environmental genomics reveals vast uncultivated protist diversity and taxonomic blind spots
Temporal dynamics of premenstrual dysphoric disorder revealed through predictive symptom networks
articles.abstract: Abstract Temporal dynamics of psychiatric symptoms challenge researchers and clinicians due to their inherent unpredictability. The cyclical on–off nature of symptoms linked to physiological rhythms, such as the menstrual cycle, provides a unique window to apply temporal and dynamic modeling of psychiatric symptoms. This can be studied in premenstrual dysphoric disorder, a female hormone-triggered condition characterized by cyclical symptoms. Yet intra-individual temporal patterns and dynamics of these symptoms remain unknown. Here we show that individuals with premenstrual dysphoric disorder differ widely in symptom timing, severity, and persistence, clustering into distinct temporal symptom profiles. Dynamic modelling uncovers temporal order among core psychiatric symptoms, with anxiety emerging as a central symptom in the unfolding of affective dysregulation. Depression shows the strongest predictive associations with subsequent severity of the other core symptoms, while irritability predicts the severity of depression at the longest time-interval. These temporal symptom dynamics reveal mechanistic psychoneuroendocrine pathways and inform precision, time-sensitive interventions for the mental health of individuals with premenstrual dysphoric disorder.

articles.title: Pico-X: a 24.9 nanowatt microcontroller for long-duration autonomous operation in flexible landing-pad sensor networks

Technological Substitution
in Pesticide Application
Reduces Occupational Risk but Fails to Mitigate Dietary Residue Burden:
Field Evidence from UAV versus Manual Spraying in Paddy Rice
articles.abstract: Abstract UAV spraying has been widely promoted as superior to manual application in Asian rice production, yet its combined implications for food safety and occupational exposure have never been evaluated within a single integrated framework. Here, we report a full-season field trial comparing UAV and manual imidacloprid (IMI) application in paddy rice, simultaneously tracking grain residue dynamics and occupational exposure in 29 applicators through to harvest. Grain IMI concentrations at harvest were comparable between regimes (86−115 μg/kg) and exceeded the EU maximum residue limit (MRL, 10 μg/kg) in both groups. More critically, on an LC-HRMS-derived relative-concentration basis, parent IMI accounted for 30.4% of the detected IMI-related profile in grain, whereas transformation products collectively accounted for 69.6%. Among these, 6-hydroxynicotinic acid was the single highest-abundance compound, surpassing parent IMI itself, yet none of the detected transformation products are included in China’s residue definition for imidacloprid in plant-derived foods. Regarding occupational exposure, urinary IMI rose approximately 9-fold from pre-exposure baseline in UAV operators compared with 17-fold in manual applicators. Manual application also induced markedly greater lipid peroxidation stress, with median baseline-normalized MDA fold changes of approximately 3.8- and 2.6-fold in the manual and UAV groups, respectively (p = 0.001). These findings establish that application technology substitution effectively reduces occupational exposure risk but confers no advantage at the food safety end point. Current parent-compound-centered residue surveillance frameworks systematically underestimate the true IMI-related burden in harvested grain, and expansion of regulatory monitoring beyond the parent compound is warranted.

articles.title:
Abnormal
Event Monitoring of Drainage Pipelines Based
on Distributed Optical Fiber Vibration Sensing
articles.abstract: Abstract Urban drainage networks are critical infrastructure for modern cities, yet their complex and concealed nature makes real-time monitoring of abnormal events a persistent challenge. To address this, this work proposed a distributed optical fiber vibration sensing system based on phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (Φ-OTDR) for drainage pipeline monitoring. To accurately capture abnormal events from complex environmental noise, a two-tier intelligent processing architecture comprising localization and classification modules was developed. The localization module employed an enhanced You Only Look Once (YOLO) model integrating anchor-box optimization, a channel-attention module, and an additional small-target feature layer, achieving a mean average precision of 96.8% in laboratory tests. The classification module utilized a hybrid model combining convolutional neural network, bidirectional long short-term memory, and attention classifier, achieving an overall accuracy of 98.1% for five abnormal events. During two-week of continuous field monitoring, the system localized simulated events with errors below 2.60 m and distinguished internal leakage, knocking, and drilling from walking, running, and vehicle interference with precision and recall exceeding 99.6% for the tested classes. Notably, the system successfully detected and accurately localized an actual branch pipe leakage event, demonstrating its practical effectiveness under real-world operating conditions.

articles.title:
Microplastics
Rapidly Sink and Beach in a Whole-Lake
Experiment
articles.abstract: Abstract Although advances in oceanographic and limnological modeling have increased our understanding of microplastic transport and persistence, we require more knowledge to effectively protect biodiversity. We initiated a whole-lake experiment (the pELAstic project) to measure the real-world fate and transport of microplastics. We added microplastics to a boreal lake, simulating stormwater input, at loading concentrations predicted to achieve environmentally relevant concentrations. Here, we introduce our experiment and describe the particle budget from the first microplastic addition. We observed rapid transport of microplastics to different ecosystem compartments. Transport patterns could not be fully explained by initial particle size and density, highlighting how natural processes modify plastic fate in real-world systems. Microplastic fragments rapidly redistributed─exiting the water column and settling on the bottom and shorelines. A particle budget across the water column, bottom sediments, and beaches accounted for 77% of the polyethylene, 48% polystyrene, and >100% polyethylene terephthalate. “Missing” plastic was likely in the nearshore littoral. Our observations suggest that if we prevent further inputs to aquatic ecosystems, microplastics will quickly disappear from the water column─washing up on shorelines and settling on the bottom. Thus, understanding rates of microplastic deposition and burial is critical to forecast the legacy of microplastic pollution.

articles.title: Issue Editorial Masthead

Extracellular
Polymeric Substances Govern Horizontal
Gene Transfer of Antibiotic Resistance Genes: Mechanisms, Pathway
Specificity, and Research Gaps
articles.abstract: Abstract The dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in environmental systems is recognized as being shaped by local matrix conditions, yet the pathway-specific role of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), the dominant matrix of biofilms, sludge flocs, and granules, remains poorly resolved. In this Review, we develop a mechanism- and pathway-resolved perspective for evaluating how EPS govern horizontal gene transfer (HGT) of ARGs. Current evidence indicates that conjugation is the most directly supported pathway, with EPS facilitating or restricting transfer through effects on donor–recipient contact, matrix organization, and transfer-related physiology. For transformation, EPS-associated extracellular ARGs constitute reservoirs, but EPS–DNA binding can both preserve genetic material and limit its immediate bioavailability. By contrast, EPS involvement in phage-mediated transduction and vesicle-mediated transfer remains mechanistically plausible but insufficiently validated. We identify five interconnected mechanisms: physical retention and spatial organization, DNA adsorption and bioavailability, regulation of intercellular contact, modulation of cell physiology and transfer competence, and community-scale mobilome coupling. By clarifying evidence boundaries across pathways, this Review moves EPS–HGT research from correlation-based interpretation toward mechanism-informed assessment of ARG mobility. We conclude by outlining research needs, including standardized EPS definition and extraction, component-resolved characterization, pathway-resolved causal assays, and validation in realistic environmental aggregates.

articles.title:
Emerging
CRISPR
Technologies for Environmental Protection:
From Genetic Engineering and Biosensing to Environmental Deployment
articles.abstract: Abstract Since its discovery, Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR) has revolutionized biomedical science and engineering with its ability to recognize and edit gene sequences with high specificity and precision. Despite the growing interest in using these capabilities to address environmental and sustainability challenges, the broader potential of CRISPR in environmental systems remains unexplored relative to its biomedical applications. Here, we provide a critical perspective on the emerging use of CRISPR for pollution management, ecological conservation, and environmental monitoring. Rather than viewing CRISPR solely as a gene-editing or biosensing technology, we consider both capabilities together to examine how advances in CRISPR engineering can translate into practical environmental solutions. We highlight the fundamental principles behind CRISPR-based editing and sensing and evaluate the challenges that constrain their transition from proof-of-concept experiments to field deployment, including off-target effects, delivery methods, ecological risks, and low sensitivity. Addressing these hurdles requires a multifaceted approach that integrates emerging technologies such as reversible CRISPR technology, amplification and cascade reactions, and machine learning, with strict regulatory oversight and rigorous risk assessments. This perspective identifies critical strengths, weaknesses, and research priorities for advancing CRISPR from laboratory technology toward robust tools for environmental applications.

articles.title:
Far-UVC
Activation of Performic Acid Enables Concurrent
Oxidative and Reductive Micropollutant Abatement
articles.abstract: Abstract Conventional UV-driven advanced oxidation and reduction processes generally emphasize one redox regime and can be inhibited by wastewater constituents. Here, we characterize the photochemistry of performic acid (PFA) under 222 and 254 nm irradiation and evaluate the capacity of PFA solution, prepared from H2O2 and formic acid and thus containing residual H2O2 and formate, to generate concurrent oxidative and reductive pathways. Relative to 254 nm, 222 nm irradiation increased the fluence-normalized photodecay rate constants of neutral PFA (PFA0) and its conjugate base (PFA–) by 1.21- and 3.81-fold, respectively. The increase arose from 16.1- and 10.1-fold larger molar absorption coefficients at 222 nm, despite lower fitted innate quantum yields (0.367 and 0.804 molecule photon–1 at 222 nm versus 0.587 and 0.819 molecule photon–1 at 254 nm). The UV222/PFA solution system generated the reductant •CO2– together with oxidative HO• and oxygen-centered organic radicals. Pathway analysis attributed 34% of carbamazepine removal to •CO2– and 19% of naproxen removal to R-O• at 222 nm. Chloride and bromide enhanced fluence-normalized degradation through reactive-halogen chemistry; the largest increases were observed for carbamazepine (47.5-fold at 254 nm and 21.9-fold at 222 nm). In real municipal wastewater, UV222/PFA solution decreased total organic carbon by 33.5% within 60 min, compared with 21.6% under UV254/PFA solution, at an initial PFA concentration of 80 μM. These results suggest far-UVC activation of PFA solution as a dual-redox treatment platform, with the observed advantages maintained in the tested wastewater effluents.

articles.title:
Chemically
Stratified
Urban Boundary Layer: Seasonally
Reversing Vertical Changes in the Underlying Chemistry of Atmospheric
Oxidation Capacity
articles.abstract: Abstract The vertical structure of atmospheric oxidation capacity (AOC) and its underlying radical chemistry within the urban boundary layer remains poorly characterized, yet it governs secondary pollutant formation. Here, we combined tower-based vertical observations with process-resolved model simulations in Beijing across winter and summer. We find that AOC generally declined with height in both seasons, but radical concentrations exhibit opposite vertical gradients. Notably, enhanced biogenic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emissions in summer suppress near-surface OH levels, creating a mid-altitude maximum. However, sharp vertical NO gradients drove an increase in ROx with height in winter. The underlying chemistry of vertical AOC variation shifts with the seasons. In winter, the photolysis of HONO dominates ROx production, and NOx-driven ROx loss prevails. In summer, the photolysis of oxygenated VOCs takes over, with radical self-reactions as the primary ROx sink. These findings demonstrate that surface observations alone may provide an incomplete representation of the whole boundary-layer chemistry.

articles.title:
Sulfur-Vacancy-Enabled
Dual-Site MoS2 Enhances
H* Utilization for Mo–H-Mediated Deep Dechlorination
articles.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical dechlorination using molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) offers a cost-effective solution for treating chlorinated organic contaminants, yet its catalytic potential remains limited by the unclear roles of Mo and S sites in mediating hydrogen utilization and C–Cl bond cleavage. Herein, we engineer sulfur-vacancy-rich MoS2 (Sv-MoS2) electrodes to expose coordinatively unsaturated Mo sites and enable an efficient Mo–H*-mediated dechlorination pathway. Using florfenicol as a model chlorinated antibiotic, Sv-MoS2 achieved near-complete dechlorination with ∼15-fold faster kinetics than pristine MoS2, reaching a rate constant of 9.26 h–1 at low energy consumption (0.0083 kWh g–1). Mechanistic analyses combining CV, EPR, in situ Raman spectroscopy, kinetic isotope effects, and DFT calculations reveal a dual-site H* utilization mechanism: S sites primarily generate H*, while vacancy-exposed Mo sites stabilize Mo–H* species that selectively drive C–Cl bond cleavage. In contrast, pristine MoS2 follows a direct electron transfer-dominated pathway and shows limited deep dechlorination. The Mo–H*-mediated pathway on Sv-MoS2 substantially lowers the energy barriers for sequential C–Cl cleavage while promoting productive H* utilization over H2 formation. The Sv-MoS2 electrode further exhibits robust performance under variable pH, natural organic matter, coexisting anions, and repeated cycling. This work clarifies Mo/S site synergy in MoS2 electrocatalysts and establishes a dual-site design framework for efficient, selective, and sustainable electrochemical hydrodechlorination.
